subtasks: S1 read-only export of the plan: Plan / PlanStep objects + an exhaustive template registry (WorkflowMode -> node sequence and dependencies), derived from build_graph()'s edges and compared against the registry in BOTH directions. ZERO change to the execution path -- no execution code reads it. Precedent for the checker: tests/unit/graph/test_conditional_edge_wiring.py introspects builder.branches and compares both halves of the edge/router contract. DELIVERED: backend/graph/plan.py (478 lines) + tests/unit/graph/test_plan_registry.py (304 lines / 24 cases); see the S1 section in prd.md. The registry declares entry + the router's per-mode vocabulary + the per-mode excluded hops rather than a hand-written node list, because the graph is mode-blind (reachable_nodes()).

S2 edges come from the plan: build_graph()'s 18 add_conditional_edges are generated from the registry/Plan, edge-for-edge equivalent, pinned by the existing structural gate plus test_routers.py (876 lines). The entry router is the main subject -- it is the only one whose destinations cannot be read statically (routers.py:80 returns a bare str) and the only member of the existing gate's _NON_LITERAL_ROUTERS exemption. DELIVERED: backend/graph/wiring.py (350 lines) + tests/unit/graph/test_wiring_registry.py (320 lines / 24 cases), plus an equivalent rewrite of builder.py, routers.py, plan.py and three existing test files; see the S2 section in prd.md. The 18 add_conditional_edges are now one loop over an exhaustive, mode-blind edge table, and _NON_LITERAL_ROUTERS is the empty set.

S3a mode registry: the 11 workflow_mode reader sites converge into the registry itself (backend/state/modes.py), and an unknown mode is refused at the request boundary instead of silently reading as 'trend'. The ticket's S3 was one large slice (Goal + convergence + refusal, risk medium-high); reconnaissance removed one premise -- "the mode is implicit in several branches" is what Goal compilation and the 11-site convergence BOTH depend on -- so S3 was split into S3a (this slice) and S3b (Goal), and the S3 row was rewritten BEFORE implementation, not after. DELIVERED: backend/state/modes.py (278 lines, ModeSpec + the two readers + mode_registry_complaints' six categories in graph/plan.py) plus four new test files (tests/unit/state/test_modes.py 21 cases, tests/unit/graph/test_modes_registry.py 13, tests/unit/api/test_workflow_mode_boundary.py 8, tests/unit/db/test_workflow_row_mode.py 5) and 3 cases added to tests/unit/api/test_status_label_reuse.py; see the S3a section in prd.md. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN: get_mode_spec raises UnknownWorkflowModeError for values that arrive from outside (a request field, a stored row) while mode_spec(state) -- the reader the routers and agents use -- is TOTAL and falls back to a declared default with a naming warning, because raising inside a graph node is the P1d shape and would make threads persisted before this module unreadable, against the P1 red line. CRITERION (ticket wording): grep -rn 'get("workflow_mode"' backend/ goes 11 -> 2, both inside the registry itself, so there are ZERO reader sites outside it.

S3b Goal becomes a first-class input: /start's initial_state literal plus the single `if req.workflow_mode == WorkflowMode.BRIEF:` special case become Goal -> compile. DELIVERED: backend/state/goal.py (155 lines: Goal + BriefInput + compile_initial_state, the only place the 24 keys are built) plus two new test files (tests/unit/state/test_goal.py 23 cases, tests/unit/api/test_start_goal.py 16), a rewrite of /start in backend/api/routes/workflow.py, four frontend files dropping the phase argument, and five repointed file:line anchors in docs/execution-plane.md; see the S3b section in prd.md. RECONNAISSANCE REMOVED A PREMISE: the literal was 24 keys, not 26, AND req.phase never decided where a run goes -- the graph's entry is always orchestrator (builder.py:149) and that node unconditionally writes mode_spec(state).initial_phase (orchestrator.py:38), so a caller-supplied phase only reached the DB row and the /start response, and both of those named a phase the graph was not in (measured: trend + phase=analyzing writes SCOUTING while answering 'analyzing'). The start phase is therefore the mode's -- one field (ModeSpec.initial_phase) now feeds the graph, the DB row and the response -- and WorkflowStartRequest.phase is removed. Backward compatibility is measured rather than assumed: pydantic's default extra='ignore' keeps a client still sending phase at 200 with an identical result. CRITERIA: grep -n 'WorkflowMode.BRIEF' backend/api/routes/workflow.py 2 -> 1, the survivor being the brief-payload input gate rather than a flow branch; the 24-key literal and req.phase are both gone. Mutation self-check: 18/18 killed, restore=OK (first run 17/18 -- M03's killer was an attribute-level test that never ran the mutated compilation line).

S4 workflow.py layering: the 7 giant endpoints split along api / application / runtime / artifacts / actions -- boundaries first, then move code, a pure move with no behaviour change, and /status staying field-for-field identical. DELIVERED: workflow.py 3001 -> 254 lines (-91.5%) over 6 layers in 5 new modules (_wf_application.py 1876, _wf_runtime.py 406, _wf_actions.py 371, _wf_artifacts.py 251, _wf_models.py 195) plus tests/unit/api/test_workflow_layering.py (6 cases); 37 files in total (31 modified + 6 new), 24 of them tests. See the S4 section in prd.md. MEASURED BASELINE (the ticket's numbers were stale: 3001 lines, not 2999, and 61 top-level symbols, not 49): the 7 giants are 1352 of 3001 lines = 45.1%, and the ticket's 47% differs by 45 lines because it counts decorators and inter-function blank lines; all seven are now 5-14 lines and workflow.py's largest function is 14 lines. THE LAYER NAMES ARE NOT INHERITED FROM AN EXISTING GATE -- an earlier design note said they were, and git grep over ec64fa86 proves it false (zero hits for all five _wf_* names). The five role names come from the ticket's own S4 row; models is the sixth layer and it is there for a structural reason, not taste: both the handler's and the implementation's annotations need the models, so putting them in application makes api <-> application a real cycle (from __future__ import annotations keeps the annotations as strings, so only pydantic's genuine evaluation closes the cycle -- it would really break). actions is likewise not a taste split: it is the two non-lease writers docs/execution-plane.md 7 already registers (_run_retry / _run_publish_retry), so the only two paths that bypass _run_graph_and_persist become a directory fact instead of a comment. THE PURE-MOVE CLAIM HAS TWO HALVES: (a) one-shot, machine-proved -- every moved symbol parses identically on both sides via ast.dump (55 symbols + 18 handler signatures, decorator_list stripped because the route decorator stays on the handler by design); that script is deliberately NOT in the repo, since it pins the moment of the move and would become dead bytes if kept; (b) permanent -- the /status shape snapshot plus 3572 passing cases. THE BIGGEST RISK WAS THE ~125 patch TARGETS: patch resolves against the namespace of the module it patches, so each target had to land on the layer that really READS the name; leaving the attribute behind after moving the read site makes the patch succeed and change nothing -- silent. Rewiring therefore picks the layer by CALL SITE, and db_update (read by both application and runtime) and _start_resume_task (read by runtime's _resume_past_evaluator_pause and by resume_workflow's own body) were decided per case, the latter keeping a _START_RESUME_LEGACY target for its legacy path. A new case asserts the ABSENCE of a re-export: if the api layer re-exported the implementation symbols, every stale patch target would silently work again. CRITERIA: (1) 7 giants 1352 lines -> all under 100 (largest function in workflow.py is 14); (2) the /status payload shape is field-for-field identical -- the SAME probe and fixture run against an ec64fa86 worktree and against this tree, with diff empty, and the only edit for the pre-split run was rewriting the patch target suffix _wf_application back to workflow. Mutation self-check: 17/17 killed, restore=OK (first run 16/17 -- M17 survived because the absence table's row floor was still >= 3 while this slice grew the table from 3 to 8 rows, so raising the floor, not adding a test, was the fix, and the comment now records that mutation found it).

S5 contract and the gate condition: docs/planning.md -- what Goal and Plan are, the evidence required before a plan may be GENERATED rather than selected (the review's 'simple tasks stay deterministic, only complex ones get planned'), and the three things this task explicitly does not do.
notes:
P2C PLANNING ROUND (feat/p2c-s1-plan-registry, commit 1ede1941) -- reconnaissance and slice plan, no code yet. The ticket was a blank placeholder (status planning, subtasks [], no prd.md, both jsonl files holding only the example line), so this round produced prd.md with sixteen findings each carrying file:line, a quantified appendix, a rewritten framing, five slices, the red lines, the refusals, the acceptance criteria and three open rulings. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: there is no owner of 'the plan'. It exists, but it is DISTRIBUTED -- 18 conditional edges x 18 routers x 11 workflow_mode readers, each re-deriving 'what happens next' from the same state bag, so nothing anywhere can answer 'what is this run going to do'. Quantified: build_graph() (builder.py:69) is a 361-line single function installing 24 nodes, 18 add_conditional_edges and 7 plain edges; routers.py has 27 top-level defs and calls _check_terminal 18 times (:82 through :598); workflow_mode has ELEVEN reader sites, EIGHT of which default to the string 'trend' (routers.py:86/431/467/541/581/605, agents/orchestrator.py:35, agents/copywriter.py:169/389, api/routes/workflow.py:968, db/workflows.py:376). The entry router (routers.py:80) is the one router whose destinations cannot be read -- it returns a bare str and is the sole member of test_conditional_edge_wiring.py:31's _NON_LITERAL_ROUTERS exemption -- and inside it the phase -> node table is written TWICE, once per mode (:90-101 brief, :104-113 trend), ending in a silent fallback (:116) that routes an unknown phase to that mode's start node. The same decision is therefore made twice: OrchestratorAgent.execute (agents/orchestrator.py:19-40, the whole file is 40 lines) compresses state into a phase by pure deterministic if-chain, and orchestrator_router expands it back into a node. SO THE TICKET'S PREMISE IS REWRITTEN: what is missing is not a Planner, it is 'the plan' as a statable object -- step one of dynamic planning is making today's implicit plan exportable, not generating a new one, and the testable criterion follows from that (given a checkpoint, can you say which nodes remain without executing the graph? today: no, you would have to simulate 18 routers). Likewise 'stop adding workflow_mode + router + edge' must become a MECHANISM (a mode missing from the registry turns a test red, following the exhaustive-registry precedent of RETRY_POLICIES / TAKEOVER_HAZARDS), not a convention. Vocabulary facts that shape the design: WorkflowMode already exists at state/enums.py:60 with exactly two members and a docstring saying 'determines starting node and pipeline path' (so the template need not be invented, only declared as data); ExecutionMode (state/enums.py:53, single/continuous) is an orthogonal axis this task must not touch; WorkflowPhase (state/enums.py:6) has 13 members of which ENGAGING is legacy (every router maps it to __end__ at :97/:110) and PLANNING means 'go to content_strategist' (:92/:106) -- so the word collides with what this task means by a plan; and TaskType (config/models.py:6) is a MODEL ROUTING KEY, so the Task object from the review's six core objects (not yet built: ArtifactRef is P1a state/artifacts.py:85, RunContext is P1b context/models.py:121, ToolResult is P1c tools/runtime/models.py:281, ActionIntent / DecisionRecord are P2a creator_agent/models.py:669/:503) must be named around it. Goal is not an object today either: 12 _run_graph_and_persist call sites across 5 files (workflow.py 7, review.py:204/:385, optimization.py:93/:157, blogger.py:118) each hand-build an initial state, and /start's is a 26-key literal (workflow.py:712-740) whose only mode difference is one `if req.workflow_mode == "brief":` at :742 gating whether the brief body goes to the Artifact Store or stays inline (:744-760). workflow.py itself is now 2999 lines (the ticket says 2519 -- it grew 480) with 49 top-level defs, the top seven holding 1397 lines (resume_workflow 327 at :1288, get_workflow_status 244 at :874, start_workflow 193 at :678, retry_publish 179 at :2821, recover_workflow 159 at :1618, retry_ripple_analysis 153 at :2159, stream_workflow_progress 142 at :1835), and each of those seven touches between two and six of seven probed concerns (DB write / events / state construction / graph execution / response body / artifacts / leases) -- start_workflow and retry_publish touch six. What makes the slices affordable: the topology ALREADY has a structural gate (test_conditional_edge_wiring.py compares a router's Literal return set against its path map at :78 and every path-map target against the real node set at :115, and its docstring records the P1d KeyError: '__end__' incident), and the graph test surface is 1581 lines across 7 files while 28 test files touch build_graph / workflow_mode / add_conditional_edges -- so an equivalence-preserving rewrite has strong tripwires, provided the reshape-do-not-delete discipline is followed point by point. BASELINE measured this round: ruff check clean, ruff format --check 520 files, mypy backend --python-version 3.12 207 files, pytest 3414 passed / 3 skipped. HONEST SCOPE NOTES: the two WorkflowPhase definitions (state/enums.py:6 as StrEnum and api/generated/models.py:49 as Enum) are member-identical 13/13 today, so this is a DUPLICATE, not a DRIFT -- registered as a latent drift surface and deliberately not merged, because nothing behaves differently and api/generated/** is a generated artifact; the plan's 31 cited anchors were verified line by line against the tree this round, and one (agents/orchestrator.py) was corrected from 22-42 to 19-40 in the process. The three open rulings are recorded in the prd: the granularity of PlanStep (node vs P1c capability -- node first, because it is exportable with zero risk, capability deferred to S3), the behaviour for an unknown Goal/mode (refuse with a named error, which is a real behaviour change needing a ruling), and whether S5 stays a document or becomes the dynamic path itself if S1-S4 produce evidence for it (follow the evidence, not the plan). status and completedAt deliberately left untouched, as is this repo's convention. P2C S1 ROUND (feat/p2c-s1-plan-registry) -- delivered backend/graph/plan.py (478 lines) + tests/unit/graph/test_plan_registry.py (304 lines / 24 cases); execution path untouched (build_graph() unchanged, no production module imports it). THE SHAPE CHANGED FROM THE TICKET'S WORDING, deliberately and on measured grounds: the ticket asked for 'WorkflowMode -> node sequence and dependencies', i.e. a hand-written per-mode node list; the graph is MODE-BLIND (24 of 24 nodes reachable from orchestrator, and the SAME 22 from either mode's entry -- reachable_nodes()), so mode membership cannot be derived from topology, and a hand-written node list would be a declaration nothing could corroborate. The registry therefore declares only entry + the router's full per-mode vocabulary + the per-mode EXCLUDED HOPS, each naming the router that decides it, and the node set is EXPORTED from build_graph(). Small enough that every part is corroborated: the five mode-conditional routers already have behaviour tests, and the entry is now corroborated by CALLING orchestrator_router -- which also closes a real gap, since its brief branch had no test at all (brief_analyzer appeared in tests only via the three ripple routers and node-level tests). THE DEFECT FOUND AND REGISTERED, NOT FIXED: orchestrator_router answers 'copywriter' for brief mode at phase=creating (routers.py:93) while builder.py:168-174's orchestrator path map has no such key; CREATING is not terminal, so the branch is reachable, and reaching it is the P1d failure mode again (a router answer with no map entry -> KeyError inside langgraph, on a path no test watches). Latent only because nothing observed reaches orchestrator with phase=creating. Fixing it means adding a map key = a behaviour change, and S1's contract is zero change, so it lives in UNRESOLVED_ROUTER_VALUES with a REVERSE assertion: once the map is fixed the exemption goes stale, plan_registry_complaints() reports exemption_no_longer_applies, and test_state_graph_and_registry_agree goes red -- so the exemption has to be deleted explicitly instead of rotting. SECOND MEASURED ASYMMETRY: Branch.ends is the path map itself ({router answer: node}), so reading it as a sequence yields ANSWERS, not DESTINATIONS; exactly one row across the 18 branches differs -- evaluator_gate's 'publisher' -> publish_gate (builder.py:394). The existing wiring test reads the keys and is CORRECT for what it checks (a router's answer must be a key), but the destination side was never checked; a keys-based export looks right on 17 of 18 branches and on the eighteenth publishes an edge the graph cannot take (evaluator_gate -> publisher, bypassing the human authorisation gate) and drops publish_gate from the plan entirely. GATES: ruff 522 files clean, ruff format --check 522, mypy 208 files clean, baseline drift within threshold, tool runtime gate OK, pytest 3438 passed 3 skipped (baseline 3414 + 24 new cases). MUTATION SELF-CHECK: 22/22 killed, 0 survived, restore=OK, plus M14 registered as an equivalent mutation (trend's plan is a strict subset of brief's, so |= and last-wins agree). Two triage findings: M11 survived twice and turned out to target DEAD CODE -- it removed followed_by's 'dst in node_set' filter, a condition that is never false because the plan is the set reachable from the root through kept edges; the condition was DELETED rather than covered, while preceded_by keeps its filter (M10 shows it is load-bearing, since a predecessor can sit outside the plan). M14 is equivalent and is labelled as such rather than papered over with a contrived test. S2 ROUND (feat/p2c-s2-edges-from-plan) -- delivered backend/graph/wiring.py (350 lines) + tests/unit/graph/test_wiring_registry.py (320 lines / 24 cases), with builder.py, routers.py, plan.py and three existing test files rewritten equivalently. THE EDGE SET IS NOW DATA: 18 hand-written add_conditional_edges calls became one loop over CONDITIONAL_EDGES, each entry declaring source + router + answers + redirects. The constructor refuses five malformed shapes (no answers, repeated answers, a redirect that is not one of the answers, a redirect to itself, source == __end__) and _by_source refuses two edges leaving one node -- langgraph permits that, but this table cannot represent it honestly, because the export reads one entry per source and the second would vanish silently. answers is DECLARED rather than derived from the router's Literal: deriving one side from the other would turn the comparison into a tautology, and the comparison is the only way either statement being wrong is discoverable -- the same contract RETRY_POLICIES and TAKEOVER_HAZARDS have. DEPARTURE FROM THE TICKET'S WORDING (registered): the ticket says the edges are 'generated from the registry/Plan', and the registry is a NEW mode-blind edge table, not PLAN_TEMPLATES -- because the graph is mode-blind (S1 measured 24/24 nodes reachable from orchestrator and the SAME 22 from either mode's entry), so edges cannot be derived from per-mode templates. The direction of truth is the reverse: the Plan is that table's projection through the graph, and PLAN_TEMPLATES still declares only which hops belong to which mode. The two declarations are joined by a new live check, entry_vocabulary_disagrees_with_the_edges: the union of the modes' declared destinations must EQUAL the entry edge's answer set, both directions. EQUIVALENCE, MEASURED: a golden snapshot of builder.branches (24 nodes / 7 plain edges / 18 branches, key order included) was written to disk BEFORE the rewrite and diffed after -- nodes 24/24 identical, plain edges 7/7 identical (StateGraph.edges is a set, so compared as sets), all 18 sources and their registered router names AND their order identical, and the path maps differ in exactly one entry: orchestrator gained copywriter -> copywriter. Branch order survived because the table is written in the order the graph used to install the edges, pinned by two assertions that are deliberately not redundant (a literal list pins the table's order; a graph-vs-table comparison pins that build_graph() walks it -- see the M16 note below). THE S1 EXEMPTION IS CLOSED: S1's UNRESOLVED_ROUTER_VALUES held (BRIEF, orchestrator_router, copywriter) because adding the map key would change behaviour; adding it is what lets the router carry an honest Literal (OrchestratorDestination), so copywriter is now a brief-only hop (TREND registers ExcludedHop('orchestrator','copywriter') -- trend's table has no CREATING key, so creating falls through to the trend_scout default) and the exemption table plus its two complaint categories were DELETED rather than left empty: their premise (a template may declare a destination the entry cannot answer) is now impossible, and an always-empty exemption table is the artifact this ticket keeps finding. THE ENTRY ROUTER IS READABLE, WHICH IS THE POINT: because its annotation was a plain str, the existing wiring gate had to skip it while every other branch was read, so the gate was one-directional (declared -> mapped) for all 18. With the annotation in place BOTH directions are read for all 18: an answer with no map entry is the P1d KeyError, and a map entry no router can return is a DEAD KEY that was never checked before. _NON_LITERAL_ROUTERS is the empty set, exactly as the ticket anticipated. REGISTERED, NOT FIXED: should_brief_or_optimize has NO CALLER AT ALL (it answers the hop after viral_matcher, but the graph reaches blogger_scout with a plain edge and has since before this table existed) -- registered in ROUTERS_WITHOUT_AN_EDGE alongside should_optimize (a real helper, called by shooting_planner_router), with a reverse assertion that wiring it up later must delete the exemption; finding it was a direct product of asking 'does every router-shaped function have an edge', which nothing had ever asked. Also registered: trend mode's phase=creating falls through the silent default to trend_scout (pre-existing, fact 5), pinned as behaviour by a test rather than fixed, because choosing a trend destination is a separate ruling. GATES: ruff check clean, ruff format --check 524 files (522 + 2 new), mypy backend --python-version 3.12 209 files clean (208 + wiring.py), baseline drift within threshold, tool runtime gate OK, pytest 3474 passed 3 skipped (3438 + 36 new cases = 24 + 2 + 3 + 7). NO EXISTING TEST WENT RED as a side effect of the rewrite. MUTATION SELF-CHECK: 22/22 killed, 0 survived, restore=OK (8/8 file hashes verified), with two first-round survivors that were NOT weak tests: (1) M16, reversing the builder's iteration, exposed that replacing one tautological order comparison with another let the middle layer through -- the fix is BOTH assertions, with docstrings stating why they are not redundant; (2) M09, making the vocabulary joint one-directional, survived because the two conditions differ only on inputs another complaint already reports, so an assertion was added that BOTH levels report a mode declaring an answer the edge does not have. The mutation harness refuses to start on an unpinned tree, preflights every anchor for uniqueness, verifies step 0 green, pins EXPECTED hashes for the untracked new files, and uses a fresh PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX plus -B per mutation so a same-second same-size edit cannot be served from stale bytecode.

S3A DELIVERED (feat/p2c-s3a-mode-registry, commit 44ad59ff, PR #620) -- the mode registry. THE SLICE WAS SPLIT BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION: the ticket's S3 bundled Goal-as-input, the 11-site convergence and the refusal of an unknown mode; the reconnaissance removed the premise they share (a mode that cannot be stated cannot be compiled), so S3a is the registry and S3b is Goal, and the S3 row in prd.md was rewritten first. WHAT THE REGISTRY IS: backend/state/modes.py declares, per WorkflowMode, the phase the orchestrator writes, the phase -> entry-node table (the two tables orchestrator_router used to hold inline, one per mode branch), the answer a ripple reangle gives and whether the mode walks the viral_matcher -> blogger_scout -> blogger_gate loop. entry is DERIVED from the IDLE route rather than declared twice, because PLAN_TEMPLATES already carries an independent declaration for plan.py to compare against. TWO READERS, DIVIDED BY WHO MAY REFUSE: get_mode_spec is strict (UnknownWorkflowModeError names the value and the alternatives) for values that come from outside; mode_spec(state) is total -- untrusted state must stay readable, so it falls back to DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_MODE and logs a warning naming the value and the thread. Missing (None) is silent and unknown is reported, which is the distinction the eight per-site "trend" defaults had erased. THE REQUEST BOUNDARY IS TIGHTENED, THE READ SURFACES ARE NOT: WorkflowStartRequest.workflow_mode is now typed WorkflowMode (pydantic answers 422 and lists the accepted values), while CheckpointSnapshot, the response models and context/models.py keep `str` -- they are the shape of stored data, and tightening them would make existing threads wrong. THE CRITERION: grep -rn 'get("workflow_mode"' backend/ goes from 11 to 2, and both hits are inside modes.py (stored_mode, mode_spec), so no reader site outside the registry remains. A new mode is one ModeSpec row; mode_registry_complaints (six categories, merged into plan_registry_complaints so that `== {}` stays the whole assertion) checks that row against the graph and against PLAN_TEMPLATES -- two independent declarations, which is the only reason comparing them can find anything. MUTATION SELF-CHECK: 26/27 killed, 0 unexpected survivors, 1 explicitly registered, restore=OK over 9 files. THE FIRST ROUND WAS 23/27 AND ALL FOUR SURVIVORS WERE THE SAME STRUCTURAL FACT: three of the nine converged sites (copywriter's brief branch, the showcase fallback, hydration's mode projection) had only "does not blow up in the default mode" tests -- their state carried no workflow_mode at all, so once the answer stopped being the literal "trend" either answer was unobservable there. The fix was to add readers, not to soften the mutants: test_execute_in_brief_mode_writes_from_the_brief, test_a_case_payload_publishes_a_mode_it_can_name (whose first-round killer was simply the wrong function -- _case_payload owns that expression, _public_result never sees a row) and test_a_threads_own_mode_survives_hydration. M23 is REGISTERED as a known gap rather than killed: the same expression in _generate_style_variants only picks the wording of a prompt, so a test for it would assert prompt text. Three harness improvements came out of this slice, all of them recorded in the skill: the anchor check is a GROUP property (declared occurrence indices must be exactly 1..N, not count == occ per entry); subprocess.run(timeout=) replaces the in-process watchdog (the restore path then always runs, instead of relying on os._exit skipping finally); and a dirty-tree refusal that really did fire once during this slice.
